recent_updates.body: Implemented multi-visual Story playback and source controls. Commit f214d2f9a2f6a49395dfa175f1e697ebb1313fae on codex/story-controls. Users can select visual sources, play sustained or timed beats, scrub, loop, replay, and return to Normal. Source preparation, overlap, replacement and disposal remain bounded. Ready for independent acceptance; not merged or installed.

- The isolated GPU probe reproduced duplicated Three/TSL failures: the second visual rendered transparent black; lighting and shader stack warnings explain the failure. [Evidence](C:/Users/zFlei/repos/lux/.worktrees/story-controls/docs/implementation/story-controls/story-interop-evidence.md).
- The reviewed [shared-linker amendment](C:/Users/zFlei/repos/lux/.worktrees/story-controls/docs/implementation/story-controls/story-shared-linker-amendment.md) adds one sealed shared dependency capsule with lazy visual entries. Standalone linking stays unchanged.
- Pure scene schemas and persistence are progressing in parallel. Scheduling remains gated on the repaired GPU probe; no user scene or installed application was changed.

- S1 is accepted at e54266c0326d56fb152d471fa54938081cfceea4 (receipt 6ac989f6-2391-40ce-af86-e3cbc199e9a5).
- Exact S2 schema, scoped resource accounting, seek/overlap behavior, and ownership are in [reviewed implementation contract](C:/Users/zFlei/repos/lux/.worktrees/story-controls/docs/implementation/story-controls/story-lifecycle-review.md#implementation-contract-addendum). This supersedes alternatives in the initial lifecycle proposal.
- First gate: independently compiled ordinary/TSL visuals must share a renderer correctly in an isolated GPU probe before scheduler implementation.

LUX-197: Native Story playback is usable in the development checkout.
Source commit: e54266c0326d56fb152d471fa54938081cfceea4.
Sustained beats hold indefinitely; scheduled occurrences have independent dwell. Timed direct beats support local seek, replay and loop. Native Story UI retains Preview, displays sequence cursor and dwell, and offers Return to Normal. Generic guarded MCP read/transport and updated installed/check-verified visual skill are connected. Scene v6 persists definitions without transient playback state.
Independent reviewer /root/review_typed_controls approved final source and actual-app UI. No remaining action finding. Original saved scene and installed Studio remain unchanged. Scheduled separate visuals are the next authorized LUX-198 slice.

# Trigger controls validation

Status: implemented and independently approved in the development worktree.
Product commits: `5c77d26c3dfdc2e4de53a0e76fea166f935d7ce5` and
`4a1742bd78d13e4c44d8dbbb57939ea272135e60`.

The Inspector exposes accessible action buttons, and `lux.studio.trigger` delivers
one acknowledged event per logical command. Same-ID retries return the original
receipt. Actions are excluded from values, saves, reset history and animation.

## Validation

Contract/compiler/component checks (116), worker checks (20), runtime routing
checks (18), UI trigger checks (3), typed UI regressions (11), and focused hostile
receipt checks passed. Root, SDK example and Studio TypeScript checks passed.
Studio test build and the actual authoring-boundary forwarding regression passed.
The shipped visual skill was installed and its installation check passed.

Native validation uses `scripts/test-studio-trigger-controls.mjs`, isolated test
profiles, native pointer/Enter/Space input, guarded MCP and a 640x360 preview.
Both relevant runs tested product `4a1742bd78d13e4c44d8dbbb57939ea272135e60`
with an empty tracked diff.

- `artifacts/studio-trigger-controls/native-1789647034497/result.json`: five
  completed criteria passed: native delivery and completed-frame receipts;
  idempotence; stale/unknown rejection; persistence/reset/build/restart without
  replay; alias/direct/selected-node isolation. Overall `ok:false` records a
  later harness race between explicit restart and automatic fault recovery.
- `artifacts/studio-trigger-controls/native-1789647267163/result.json`: focused
  fault/recovery tail passed (`ok:true`). Authored failure emits no receipt,
  rejects redelivery, preserves saved bytes, and recovers generation 3 to 4 with
  an empty ledger. Before/failure/recovery canvas PNGs are byte-identical SHA256
  `f0366541ef0f34ce422827c1e33dcbac8dff961e0949f47507e0edd40350959f`.

This is composite acceptance, not a claim of one fully green end-to-end run.
The final harness SHA256 is
`6da70f20117eb98ac4513a29cacf16b1ad12fcfcdc96753acdeb60f32212a1c3`.
All owned Studio processes exited. No user process was touched.

Independent reviewer `/root/review_typed_controls` approved source, contracts,
runtime, UI and this composite evidence with no actionable findings. Screenshots
in the main run include `wide-trigger-controls.png`, `narrow-trigger-controls.png`
and `component-trigger-isolation.png`. The 1360x900 and 820x720 views (242px
Inspector) passed hierarchy, readability, keyboard and overflow review.

## Delivery boundary

Development branch only; installed Studio and user scenes remain unchanged.
Numeric Resolume export remains supported; trigger schemas reject before packaging.
No remaining implementation QA is required for this slice. Integration is separate.

LUX-195 implemented in the isolated story-controls worktree. Authors can use numeric, boolean and enum values through native Inspector and generic MCP; save/reopen preserves values, and component instances remain independent. Numeric modulation and export stay supported; typed export fails precisely before packaging. Source/UI review approved. Integration and installed-app replacement remain separate.
